# Road transport {#sec-transport}

Road transport is the largest user of oil products in most countries, and the place where carbon pricing meets a
slow-moving capital stock: cars, trucks and motorcycles last ten or twenty years, and the choice between a petrol car
and an electric one is made once, at purchase. The model offers two ways to project road fuel use.

- **The elasticity model** (the default). Road gasoline, diesel, LPG and natural gas follow the same constant-elasticity
  fuel-use equation as every other sector and fuel ([M3.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M3-1)); it is described in
  @sec-demand.
- **The engineer road model** (switched on per scenario with `TrModel`). It projects the vehicle fleet itself:
  how many vehicles people own, how many they buy and scrap, whether they buy electric, how efficient the new vehicles
  are and how far they are driven. Fuel use follows from vehicles, distance and fuel economy.

This chapter describes the engineer model: what it is (@sec-tr-what), its data (@sec-tr-data), how it computes one
year (@sec-tr-ownership to @sec-tr-results), its caveats (@sec-tr-caveats), and how it compares with legacy CPAT
(@sec-tr-legacy). The implementation in Excel-AI and CPAT Python closes the chapter (@sec-tr-impl).

The CPAT methodology describes the elasticity approach in
[section 3.3.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-FuelConsumptionDynamics); it has no chapter on
the engineer road model, whose source is the legacy CPAT workbook and its methodology note
(`Transportation_methodology.docx`). The methodology's road transport module
([chapter 7](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/07_Road_Transport.html#summary)) is related but different: it projects
vehicle-kilometres, congestion, accidents and road damage from fuel prices with estimated elasticities
([section 7.3.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/07_Road_Transport.html#vehicle-kilometers-traveled-vkt),
[section 7.3.8](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/07_Road_Transport.html#sec-methodo)), for the co-benefits of
@sec-fiscal. The engineer model sends its road fuel use to that module (@sec-tr-results).

## Two road models and the switch {#sec-tr-what}

The two road models are computed side by side in every scenario. The switch only decides which one the rest of the
model reads.

| | Elasticity model (default) | Engineer road model |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of analysis | Fuel use by fuel | Vehicles by class and powertrain |
| Behaviour | Income, price and efficiency elasticities, autonomous efficiency gain | Ownership in income, total cost of ownership (TCO), logit choice of EVs, fuel economy, distance driven |
| Electric vehicles | Road electricity grows with the transport demand multiple of the power model | Explicit: BEV and PHEV stocks, their electricity use |
| Policies that act | Carbon tax, excise, fuel price reform, regulations (through prices and shadow prices) | The same through fuel prices, plus feebates, distance tax, EV subsidy, purchase taxes, VAT and customs on BEVs, charging-station subsidy |
| Chapter | @sec-demand | This chapter |

**The switch.** `TrModel` on ScenarioDefinition (one value per scenario, default `Elasticity`). The flag

$$
sw^{T} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{TrModel starts with "Engineer"} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-switch}

decides, in every year, which fuel use the rest of the model reads ([M3.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M3-2)):

$$
F_{rod,f,t} = \begin{cases} F^{T}_{f,t} & sw^T = 1 \text{ and } f \in \{\text{gasoline, diesel, LPG, natural gas, biofuels}\} \\ F^{e}_{rod,f,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-fuelswitch}

where

- $F^{T}_{f,t}$ is road fuel use of the engineer model (ktoe, @eq-tr-ktoe and @eq-tr-bio), `trkt`, `trbio`;
- $F^{e}_{rod,f,t}$ is road fuel use of the elasticity model (ktoe), `enel` (biofuels: `trbe`);
- $F_{rod,f,t}$ is the road fuel use used everywhere else, `ener`.

Road electricity enters power demand ([M4.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M4-1), @sec-power) the same way:

$$
E_{rod,t} = \begin{cases} E^{T}_{t} & sw^T = 1,\ t > t_0 \\ E_{rod,t-1}\, m_{tra,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-elswitch}

where $E^{T}_{t}$ is road electricity of the engineer model (ktoe, `trkte`, @eq-tr-ktoe-el), $m_{tra,t}$ the growth
multiple of the transport demand group in the power model, and $t_0$ the base year (2022). In the base year road
electricity is the data under both models.

With the engineer model on, CO2, methane, local air pollutants, revenues and all totals follow the engineer road fuel
use, because they are computed from $F_{rod,f,t}$. With the default, every result is exactly the elasticity model's.

**What the engineer model covers.** Road gasoline, diesel, LPG, natural gas (CNG and LNG) and electricity, and the road
biofuels, which follow gasoline and diesel (@eq-tr-bio). Coal, kerosene and other oil products in road, and rail,
aviation and navigation, stay on the elasticity model whatever the switch says.

**No circular reference.** The engineer model reads last year's power price, last year's GDP growth and this year's
GDP level after the GDP feedback (which uses last year's effect); fuel prices do not depend on fuel use. So switching it
on adds no loop to the year.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P[Fuel prices and taxes<br/>section 2, sections 5-8] --> E[Engineer road model<br/>section 5b]
  W[Last year's power price<br/>section 3] --> E
  G[GDP per capita, population] --> E
  E -->|TrModel = Engineer| F[Road fuel use ener]
  L[Elasticity model enel] -->|TrModel = Elasticity| F
  E -->|TrModel = Engineer, t > base year| D[Road electricity demand<br/>power model]
  E --> C[Transport co-benefits<br/>always]
  F --> R[CO2, pollutants, revenues, totals]
```

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: the road switch"}
```
for t in years:
    tr_sw = 1 if TrModel[scenario].startswith("Engineer") else 0
    for f in ["gso", "die", "lpg", "nga", "bio"]:
        ener[rod, f, t] = trkt_or_trbio[f, t] if tr_sw == 1 else enel_or_trbe[rod, f, t]
    if tr_sw == 1 and t > base_year:
        dem[rod, t] = trkte[t]                      # road electricity of the engineer model
    else:
        dem[rod, t] = dem[rod, t-1] * mult[transport group, t]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: the switch"}
- **Excel-AI:** `TrModel` is ScenarioDefinition row 338 (legacy MTInputs F340, Dashboard G61). Mitigation row `tr.sw`
  (`ENGINEERON`). Section 5: `ener` = `ROADSWITCH($D, tr.sw, result rows trkt/trbio, enel)`, where column D is the
  Inputs column `trpos`: the position of the fuel in `TrFuelKey` for road (gasoline 1, diesel 2, LPG 3, gas 4,
  biofuels 6), 0 elsewhere. `ROADSWITCH` also adds the cumulative residential leakage to biomass of section 6b.
  Section 3 H: `dem` = `DEMROAD($F, tr.sw, trkte, previous, multiple)`, where F is the Inputs_power column `tr`
  (1 for road). The elasticity fuel use is the variable `enel` (the former `ener` formula, `FUELUSE`, base year from
  Inputs); with `TrModel` = Elasticity `ener` = `enel` everywhere, so every elasticity-model output is unchanged
  (regression 0).
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/road.py`, `prepare()` and `step()` (equations A3.5-A3.9). Python computes
  the engineer model in every scenario for the transport co-benefits module, but `TrModel` = Engineer is **not yet
  supported**: `road.prepare` raises `NotImplementedError` ("road fuel use of sections 3 and 5 from the engineer
  model"). See the [CPAT Python blocks](../CPAT_coded_documentation_html/02_How_it_works.html#sec-blocks).
:::

## The engineer model at a glance {#sec-tr-glance}

The engineer model is the "technoeconomic" road model of legacy CPAT. It works in vehicles per thousand people, one
year at a time, for four vehicle classes and two powertrain families.

| Class | Code | Powertrains | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Passenger and light vehicles, bought new | `pas` | Gasoline, diesel, LPG, CNG ICEVs; PHEVs; BEVs | Cars and light vehicles blended by their ownership shares |
| Passenger and light vehicles, bought used | `pau` | ICEV, BEV | Imported or second-hand; their own TCO and choice |
| Freight vehicles | `fre` | Diesel, LPG, LNG trucks; BEV trucks | No VAT on the purchase price (as legacy) |
| 2-3 wheelers | `cyc` | Gasoline; BEV | Ownership follows a hump in income |
| Buses | `bus` | Diesel, LPG, gas; electricity | Fuel use only: scaled with passenger fuel use |

**One year of the model** runs in this order. Each step has its section below.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A[Prices, income, discount rate] --> B[Opening stock, retirements]
  B --> C[Charging stations, mark-up, range anxiety]
  C --> D[Fuel economy of new vehicles, feebate per liter]
  D --> E[Distance for the purchase decision]
  E --> F[Total cost of ownership per km]
  F --> G[Ownership demand, purchases]
  G --> H[EV choice logit, ICE fuel split]
  H --> I[Closing stock, vehicles by fuel]
  I --> J[Stock fuel economy, distance, fuel use]
  J --> K[Calibration to the energy balance, buses]
  K --> L[Road fuel and electricity use, results]
```

**Notation.** The methodology has no symbols for the road model, so this chapter uses its own (Excel-AI notation,
as the equation list, [M5](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M5-1)). Every equation holds for each scenario and country; the
indices $o$ and $c$ are omitted. Vehicle class is $k$, ICE fuel $f$, year $t$, base year $t_0$.

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| $y_t$ | GDP per capita (real GDP after the GDP feedback / population) | USD | `trgpc` |
| $N_t$ | Population | million | `trpop` |
| $O_{k,t}$ | Vehicle ownership | per 1,000 people | `trdmcp`, `trdmcf`, `trdmcc` |
| $S^{o}, S^{a}, S^{cl}$ | Opening stock, stock after retirement, closing stock | per 1,000 people | `trop*`, `traft*`, `trclo*` |
| $u_t$ | Share of used vehicles in passenger purchases | share | `trush` |
| $L_k$ | Useful life: passenger 20, freight 10, 2-3 wheeler 7 | years | `trp.life` |
| $n$ | Years a new passenger vehicle is owned before resale (7) | years | `trp.life` |
| $fe$ | Fuel economy | km per liter (BEV: km per kWh) | `trfn`, `trfsc` |
| $v$ | Distance per vehicle | km a year | `trvkn`, `trvkc` |
| $p_f$ | Fuel price incl. all taxes and new policies | USD per liter | `trprl` |
| $r_t$ | Consumer discount rate | share | `trdisc` |
| $K$ | Discounted distance over the ownership period | km | `trdkm*` |
| $TCO$, $c$ | Total cost of ownership; TCO per km | USD; USD per km | `trto*`, `trpk*` |
| $s^{EV}$ | EV share of purchases | share | `trevsh`, `trshfb`, `trshcb` |
| $B$ | Distance driven | billion km | `trbkm` |
| $F$ | Fuel use | billion liters (results: ktoe) | `trfup`, `trkt` |

## Data {#sec-tr-data}

The engineer model needs much more data than the elasticity model: the size and make-up of the fleet, the fuel
economy and distance of each vehicle type, vehicle prices and taxes. All of it is held for every country and looked up
by the country code, so changing the country changes the whole road model.

| Data | Content | Lookup | Legacy source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transport1 | 220 countries, data years 2022-2025: shares of road fuel use by vehicle type, fuel economy, ownership, EV shares of purchases and of the stock, distance per vehicle, used-vehicle share, import duties and shares, charging stations, ownership saturation | ISO code and variable (`TrKey` = country\|variable) | Transport1 (`transport_data.csv`) |
| Transport2 | Purchase prices of ICEVs and EVs (passenger, freight, 2-3 wheeler), 2022-2040; a year without a price holds the last one | ISO code | Transport2 (`vehicle_prices.csv`) |
| Transport3 | Range anxiety by class, the start value of @eq-tr-ra (fitted, @sec-tr-charging), with the actual and calculated EV shares of the fit year; 194 countries | Country name; the average of the table if the country has no value | Transport3 (`range_anxiety.csv`) |
| TransportParams | Lifetimes, depreciation, insurance, maintenance, elasticities, logit $k$, ownership (Gompertz, adjustment, limits), charging, discount rate, data years; the methodology note's alternative values (not used) | Key | Legacy side tables and Dashboard (`transport_params.csv`) |
| TransportPaths | BEV fuel economy of the stock (light, freight, 2-3 wheeler), charging cost per port, 2022-2041 | Key and year | Legacy Mitigation rows 2051, 2095, 2122, 2170 (`transport_paths.csv`) |
| Manual inputs J374:AC377 | BEV fuel economy of new vehicles (km per kWh; passenger and light, freight, 2-3 wheeler; 2022-2041), read by label (D375:D377) and year (row 374) | Label and year | Legacy Manual inputs, same cells |
| Fuel table (Inputs) | GJ per liter, CO2 per GJ, road usage and efficiency elasticities, autonomous efficiency gain, base-year road fuel use (energy balance), road biofuels and electricity | Fuel and subsector | Inputs, energy balance |

**Data years.** A year is a *data year* when Transport1 has it (2022-2025). In data years the model takes the data
(ownership, stocks, EV shares, fuel economy, distance) wherever legacy has `IF(ISNUMBER(data), data, model)`; from
2026 it projects. A blank Transport1 cell counts as no data.

**Base-year split of road fuel.** Transport1 gives, for each fuel, the share used by each vehicle type in the first
data year. Light vehicles take the rest
([A3.5](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-5)):

$$
Q_{k,f} = sh_{k,f}\, F^{bal}_{f,t_0}, \qquad L_{k,f} = Q_{k,f}\, \lambda_f / 10^{9}, \qquad sh_{lgt,f} = 1 - \sum_{k \ne lgt} sh_{k,f}
$$ {#eq-tr-split}

where

- $sh_{k,f}$ is the share of fuel $f$ used by vehicle type $k$ (passenger, 2-3 wheeler, bus, freight), `trshf`;
- $F^{bal}_{f,t_0}$ is base-year road use of the fuel in the energy balance (ktoe), `trp.eb`;
- $\lambda_f$ is liters per ktoe (natural gas counted in liters of gasoline equivalent, as legacy), `trp.lpk`;
- $Q_{k,f}$ and $L_{k,f}$ are the base-year fuel use of the type in ktoe and billion liters, `trp.bsh`.

Gasoline is split between passenger vehicles, 2-3 wheelers and light vehicles; diesel, LPG and gas between passenger,
bus, freight and light vehicles.

**Purchase taxes from the data.** VAT on vehicles is the general VAT rate of the customs data year (`VAT_WEO`, from
the domestic price data); freight vehicles pay no VAT, as legacy. Import duties on ICEVs and BEVs are those of the
customs data year (2024), import shares those of the import data year (2022); 2-3 wheelers use the passenger import
share. **Bus electricity** in the base year is the passenger EV stock share of 2024 times base-year bus fuel.

### Inputs from the rest of the model {#sec-tr-inputs}

The engineer model reads prices and income from the other blocks.

| Input | Definition | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Road fuel price | After-tax road price incl. new policies (USD per GJ, @sec-prices) × GJ per liter | `trprl` |
| Road gas price | After-tax road gas price per GJ / 26 liters per GJ (USD per liter equivalent) | `trprg` |
| PHEV price | $\phi\, p_{gso} + (1 - \phi)\, p^{EV}_{res} \times 9$ kWh per liter, $\phi$ the gasoline share of PHEV distance | `trpphv` |
| Industrial gas (LNG trucks) | Industrial gas price before new policies + the road new policies × (1 + VAT), at least the price floor (USD per GJ) | `trpri` |
| Freight fuel prices | Road prices net of VAT (LNG: industrial gas net of VAT / 26) | `trprn`, `trprm` |
| GDP per capita | Real GDP after the GDP feedback (@sec-fiscal) / population | `trgpc` |
| Lagged GDP growth | GDP growth of the previous year (base year: WEO growth of the year before) | `trgdl` |
| Electricity price | End-user price of the previous year, residential and industrial (@sec-power) | `rp` |
| Regulation shadow price | Road regulation shadow price (USD per tCO2) | `reg.rod` |

The **consumer discount rate** falls linearly with income between two thresholds:

$$
r_t = \min\!\left(r^{max},\ \max\!\left(r^{min},\ r^{max} - \frac{y_t - y^{lo}}{y^{hi} - y^{lo}}\,(r^{max} - r^{min})\right)\right)
$$ {#eq-tr-disc}

where $r^{max} = 15\%$ at $y^{lo} = 1{,}000$ USD and $r^{min} = 5\%$ at $y^{hi} = 50{,}000$ USD (`disc_max`,
`disc_inc_low`, `disc_min`, `disc_inc_high`). It discounts passenger, freight and 2-3 wheeler costs alike.

| Charging stations: elasticity to the BEV stock; to their cost | 0.3; −0.67 | `ch_el_stock`, `ch_el_cost` |
| Charging mark-up: maximum, minimum (USD per kWh); EV share at the minimum; public share | 0.3; 0.02; 0.5; 0.2 | `ch_cost_max`, `ch_cost_min`, `ch_sat`, `ch_public` |

| Gas liters per GJ; PHEV kWh per liter | 26; 9 | `gas_l_per_gj`, `phev_l_per_kwh` |

The own- and cross-TCO elasticities are legacy literals: the averages of (−1.72, −1.27, −1.08, −0.99) and
(0.71, 0.43, 0.51, 0.64). The distance (usage) and new-fuel-economy (efficiency) elasticities, and the autonomous
efficiency gain, are the road gasoline and diesel values of the fuel table (@sec-demand): passenger vehicles and
2-3 wheelers use gasoline's, freight diesel's.

**The methodology note's alternatives** are stored with the parameters but not used; they are candidates for a later
review.

| Parameter | Legacy (used) | Methodology note |
|---|---|---|
| Consumer discount rate, low / high income | 15% / 5% | 30% / 10% |
| Income elasticity of distance | 0.1 (2-3 wheeler −0.4) | 0.05 |
| Driving elasticity, light vehicles and 2-3 wheelers | −0.4 (road gasoline) | −0.3 |
| Driving elasticity, heavy vehicles | −0.3 (road diesel) | −0.2 |
| EV maintenance | ICEV × 2/3 | ICEV × 1/3 |
| BEV / ICEV distance in the TCO | cap 1.2 | identical |
| Maximum charging mark-up | 0.3 USD per kWh | 0.10 USD per kWh |
| Maintenance cost | fixed USD per km | rises with wages |
| ICEV prices | Transport2 path | rise with income |

### Data-year quantities {#sec-tr-datayears}

In the data years the model turns the Transport1 data into the quantities it needs. Passenger cars and light vehicles
are blended by the passenger share of their ownership,

$$
\sigma = \frac{O^{data}_{pas}}{O^{data}_{pas} + O^{data}_{lgt}}, \qquad x_{mix} = \sigma\, x_{pas} + (1 - \sigma)\, x_{lgt}
$$ {#eq-tr-blend}

which gives the blended fuel economy (LPG and CNG light vehicles scaled by $fe_{pas,f}/fe_{pas,gso}$), BEV fuel
economy, distance, and EV shares of the stock and of purchases (`trsps`, `trfem`, `trfem2`, `trfebm`, `trvkm`,
`trevom`, `trevpm`). From them:

- **PHEV distance share** $\phi = fe_{gso}/fe_{phv}$, the share of PHEV distance on gasoline; PHEV share of distance
  = (EV − BEV stock share) × $\phi$ × $\sigma$.
- **Distance by fuel** = fuel economy × base-year fuel (billion liters, @eq-tr-split), held from the base year; the
  **vehicle shares by fuel** are this distance split × (1 − EV stock share). The base-year split is used in every
  data year.
- **BEV distance**: ICEV distance × $\min\!\big(cap, (c^{BEV}/c^{ICE})^{\epsilon_U}\big)$, the cost-per-km ratio of a
  BEV to a gasoline car (prices before new policies; last year's residential power price) raised to the usage
  elasticity, capped (`trbvu`).
- **Freight distance per vehicle** in the base year = diesel freight distance / (diesel vehicle share × freight
  ownership × population); in later data years it moves with the passenger distance ratio (`trvkfd`).
- **Stocks** by class and powertrain = ownership × (1 − BEV stock share) for ICEVs, the rest for BEVs (`trstd`).
- **Ownership years** of a passenger vehicle $= u\,L_{pas} + (1-u)\,n$ (`trowny`), with $u$ the used share (data,
  then held).

The **freight share of ownership** is freight ownership over passenger and light ownership in data years; after the
last data year it falls with income towards its target, capped at the last-data-year value $\nu$:

$$
\phi^{fre}_t = \min\!\left(\nu,\ \max\!\left(\phi^{*},\ \nu - (\nu - \phi^{*})\,\frac{y_t}{y^{*}}\right)\right)
$$ {#eq-tr-fsh}

where $\phi^{*} = 0.0236$ is the target share and $y^{*} = 87{,}398$ USD the income at which it is reached.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: data"}
- **Excel-AI:** data sheets in the DATA group: Transport1 (`TrKey`, `TrVal`, `TrYr`), Transport2 (`VPKey`, `VPVal`,
  `VPYr`), Transport3 (`RAKey`, `RAPas`, `RAFre`, `RACyc`, `RAPasA`, `RAPasC`, `RAFreA`, `RAFreC`, `RACycA`,

  inputs J374:AC377 (rows `trfen`). Mitigation section 5b: parameter rows `trp.*` (D:G), key inputs `trshf` ...
  `trvp` (Transport1 lookups, blank = 0; paths; vehicle prices, last price carried), derived parameters `trp.bsh`,
  `trp.tax`, `trp.bus`, inputs from the model `trprl` ... `trdisc`, data-year derivations `trsps` ... `trstdc`
  (held values `trnc`, `trjc`: the last data year). The data come from `extract_transport.py`, which reads the legacy

- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/road_data.py`: `params`, `data_years`, `country_rows`, `path_rows`,

## Vehicle ownership and its calibration {#sec-tr-ownership}

Ownership is the backbone of the model: how many vehicles per thousand people a country wants at its income. It
follows an S-shaped Gompertz curve in GDP per capita, scaled so that it passes through the observed ownership, and
the fleet moves only part of the way towards it each year
([M5.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M5-1), [A3.6](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-6)).

**The Gompertz target** for passenger and light vehicles:

$$
O^{*}_{pas,t} = \overline{S}\,(1 - \phi^{fre}_t)\; e^{\,a\, e^{\,b\, y_t/1000}}\; J_{pas}
$$ {#eq-tr-gompertz}

where

- $\overline{S}$ is the ownership saturation point (vehicles per 1,000 people, Transport1, held after the data years),
  `trsat`;
- $\phi^{fre}_t$ is the freight share of ownership (@eq-tr-fsh);
- $a = -5.897$ and $b = -0.23$ per 1,000 USD are the Gompertz constants;
- $J_{pas}$ is the calibration factor (@eq-tr-calib), `trjjp`.

Freight uses the same curve with $\overline{S}\,\phi^{fre}_t$ in place of $\overline{S}\,(1-\phi^{fre}_t)$ and its own
$J_{fre}$.

**Calibration to observed ownership.** In each data year the model compares actual ownership with the curve; the
factor of the last data year is held for all later years:

$$
J_k = \frac{O^{data}_{k,T}}{\overline{S}\,(1 - \phi^{fre}_{T})\, e^{\,a\, e^{\,b\, y_{T}/1000}}}, \qquad T = \text{last data year (2025)}
$$ {#eq-tr-calib}

The factor works both ways: a country below the curve stays below it. For Egypt, ownership was 55 per 1,000 in 2025
against a Gompertz level of 152, so $J = 0.36$.

**Partial adjustment and limits.** Desired ownership moves a fraction $\mu$ of the way to the target, and actual
ownership may grow or fall only within limits:

$$
\tilde{O}_{k,t} = \mu\, O^{*}_{k,t} + (1 - \mu)\, O_{k,t-1}
$$ {#eq-tr-partial}

$$
O_{k,t} = \begin{cases} S^{data}_{k,ICE,t} + S^{data}_{k,BEV,t} & \text{data year} \\ \max\!\Big(O_{k,t-1}(1 - d_k),\ \min\big(O_{k,t-1}(1 + g_k),\ \tilde{O}_{k,t}\big)\Big) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-own}

where $\mu = 0.09$ (`own_adj`), $g_k = 7.5\%$ the maximum annual growth and $d_k = 10\%$ the maximum annual decline
(`TrOwnDecline` for passenger and freight, `own_max_decline` for 2-3 wheelers). This is the only partial-adjustment
equation of the model.

**2-3 wheelers** follow a hump in income instead of a Gompertz curve, without partial adjustment ($\mu = 1$). With
$H = 7{,}000$ USD the income of the peak and $\kappa = 0.737$ a scale factor:

$$
J^{cyc} = O^{data}_{cyc,T}\left(1 + \kappa\Big(1 - \frac{y_T}{H}\Big)\right), \qquad O^{*}_{cyc,t} = \frac{2\, J^{cyc}}{y_t/H + H/y_t} = \frac{2\,J^{cyc}\,H\,y_t}{y_t^2 + H^2}
$$ {#eq-tr-hump}

$J^{cyc}$ is the peak level, set from the last data year $T$ and held. The target then enters @eq-tr-own with the
2-3 wheeler limits.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: ownership"}
```
for t in years:
    if data_year(t):
        J_pas = own_data[pas, t] / (sat * (1 - fsh[t]) * exp(a * exp(b_pas * gpc[t] / 1000)))
        J_fre = own_data[fre, t] / (sat * fsh[t] * exp(a * exp(b_fre * gpc[t] / 1000)))
        J_cyc = own_data[cyc, t] * (1 + scale * (1 - gpc[t] / peak))
    # (held after the last data year)
    target[pas] = sat * (1 - fsh[t]) * exp(a * exp(b_pas * gpc[t] / 1000)) * J_pas_prev
    target[fre] = sat * fsh[t] * exp(a * exp(b_fre * gpc[t] / 1000)) * J_fre_prev
    target[cyc] = 2 * J_cyc_prev / (gpc[t] / peak + peak / gpc[t])
    for k in ["pas", "fre", "cyc"]:
        if stock_data[k, t] > 0:
            own[k, t] = stock_data[k, ICE, t] + stock_data[k, BEV, t]
        else:
            adj = 1 if k == "cyc" else own_adj[k]
            desired = adj * target[k] + (1 - adj) * own[k, t-1]
            own[k, t] = max(own[k, t-1] * (1 - decline[k]),
                            min(own[k, t-1] * (1 + max_growth[k]), desired))
```
:::

- **Excel-AI:** Mitigation section 5b, demand block: `trjhp`, `trjip`, `trjjp` (passenger expected, actual,
  factor, held), `trjhf`, `trjif`, `trjjf` (freight), `trsatp`, `trsatq`, `trgtp` (`GOMPTGT`), `trdemp` (`OWNDEM`),
  `trdmcp` (`CLAMPOWN`); freight `trsatf`, `trsatg`, `trgtf`, `trdemf`, `trdmcf`; 2-3 wheelers `trjc`, `trcyh`
  (`CYCHUMP`), `trdmcc`; freight share `trnc`, `trfsh` (`FRESHARE`). Parameters `trp.own`, `trp.ogr`, `trp.odc`
  (decline: named constant `TrOwnDecline` = 0.1), `trp.frs`.
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_year()`, block "vehicle ownership" (`demand()`); equation M5.1, A3.6.

## The stock: retirements, purchases and the closing stock {#sec-tr-stock}

Each year some vehicles are scrapped and new ones are bought to reach the ownership of @eq-tr-own. The stock is
followed separately for new and used passenger vehicles, freight vehicles and 2-3 wheelers, each split into ICEVs and
BEVs ([A3.6](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-6)).

**Opening stock.** In a data year it is the data (passenger: × the new or used share); otherwise last year's closing
stock:

$$
S^{o}_{k,v,t} = \begin{cases} S^{data}_{k,v,t}\, w_k & \text{data year} \\ S^{cl}_{k,v,t-1} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-open}

where $v$ is ICE or BEV and $w_{pas} = 1 - u_t$, $w_{pau} = u_t$, $w_{fre} = w_{cyc} = 1$.

**Retirement** is the average opening stock of the last years over the life, at most the stock itself:

$$
R_{k,v,t} = \min\!\left(\frac{1}{L_k}\cdot\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=0}^{m-1} S^{o}_{k,v,t-j},\ \ S^{o}_{k,v,t}\right), \qquad m = \min(L_k,\ t - t_0 + 1)
$$ {#eq-tr-retire}

with lives $L_{pas} = n = 7$ (a new passenger vehicle is resold after seven years), $L_{pau} = 20 - 7 = 13$,
$L_{fre} = 10$ and $L_{cyc} = 7$. The stock after retirement is $S^{a} = S^{o} - R$.

**Purchases** fill the gap between ownership and the stock that remains; passenger purchases are split between new
and used vehicles by the used share:

$$
P_{k,t} = O_{k,t} - \sum_{v} S^{a}_{k,v,t}, \qquad P_{pas,t}^{new} = (1 - u_t)\, P_{pas,t}, \qquad P_{pau,t} = u_t\, P_{pas,t}
$$ {#eq-tr-purchase}

The purchases of each powertrain are the class purchases × its share from the choice of @sec-tr-choice.

**Closing stock.** In data years a balancing item makes the closing stock equal the data; afterwards it is zero:

$$
S^{cl}_{k,v,t} = S^{a}_{k,v,t} + s_{k,v,t}\, P_{k,t} + \Delta_{k,v,t}, \qquad \Delta_{k,v,t} = \begin{cases} S^{data}_{k,v,t}\, w_k - S^{a}_{k,v,t} - s_{k,v,t}\, P_{k,t} & \text{data year} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-close}

where $s_{k,v,t}$ is the purchase share of the powertrain. The BEV stock in million vehicles,
$\sum_k S^{o}_{k,BEV}\,N/1000$, drives the charging stations of @sec-tr-charging; the EV share of the opening passenger
stock drives the charging mark-up.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: the stock"}
```
for t in years:
    for k in ["pas", "pau", "fre", "cyc"]:
        for v in ["ice", "bev"]:
            if stock_data[k, v, t] > 0:
                opening[k, v, t] = stock_data[k, v, t] * share_of_class[k]
            else:
                opening[k, v, t] = closing[k, v, t-1]
            m = min(life[k], t - base_year + 1)
            retired[k, v, t] = min(mean(opening[k, v, t-m+1 : t+1]) / life[k], opening[k, v, t])
            after[k, v, t] = opening[k, v, t] - retired[k, v, t]
    # ... ownership (previous section) and choice (below) ...
    buy[pas] = own[pas, t] - sum(after[pas|pau, :, t]);  buy_new = (1 - used_share) * buy[pas]
    buy_used = buy[pas] - buy_new;  buy[fre] = own[fre, t] - sum(after[fre, :, t]);  ...
    for k, v:
        purchases[k, v, t] = share[k, v, t] * buy[k]
        plug = stock_data[k, v, t] * share_of_class[k] - after[k, v, t] - purchases[k, v, t] if data else 0
        closing[k, v, t] = after[k, v, t] + purchases[k, v, t] + plug
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: the stock"}
- **Excel-AI:** Mitigation section 5b, stock block: `tropn`, `tropu`, `tropf`, `tropc` (`OPENING`), `travn` ...
  `travc` (`TRAILAVG`), `trretn` ... `trretc` (`RETIRED`), `traftn` ... `traftc`, `trbuyn` ... `trbuyc`,
  `trplgn` ... `trplgc` (`PLUG`), `trclon` ... `trcloc`; `trstt`, `trevst`, `trevsf`, `trevsc`, `trafts`, `traftsf`,
  `traftsc`, `trbevm`; purchases `trbyt`, `trbytn`, `trbytu`, `trbytf`, `trbytc`.
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_year()`, blocks "the stock at the start of the year" and "purchases, the gap to the data
  stock, closing stock".

## Charging, the charging mark-up and range anxiety {#sec-tr-charging}

Electric vehicles face two costs that petrol cars do not: a mark-up for public charging, and *range anxiety*, the
money-equivalent of the fear of running out of charge. Both fall as electric vehicles spread and charging stations are
built.

**Charging-station subsidy** (policy scenarios only): zero before its start year, linear to the target level, then
constant:

$$
\varsigma_t = \pi_t \cdot \begin{cases} 0 & t < t^{cs}_{0} \\ \varsigma_0 + (\varsigma_1 - \varsigma_0)\min\!\left(1,\ \dfrac{t - t^{cs}_0}{\max(1,\ t^{cs}_1 - t^{cs}_0)}\right) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-cssub}

where $\pi_t$ is 1 in a policy scenario (scenario number above 1) and 0 in the baseline, $t^{cs}_0, \varsigma_0$ the
start year and level, $t^{cs}_1, \varsigma_1$ the target year and level (`TrCsStartYear`, `TrCsStartLevel`,
`TrCsTargetYear`, `TrCsTargetLevel`). The cost per charging port after the subsidy is $C_t = C^{port}_t(1-\varsigma_t)$.

**Charging stations** are the data in data years, then grow with the BEV stock and fall with their cost:

$$
H_t = H_{t-1}\left(\frac{V^{BEV}_t}{V^{BEV}_{t-1}}\right)^{0.3}\left(\frac{C_t}{C_{t-1}}\right)^{-0.67}
$$ {#eq-tr-stations}

where $V^{BEV}$ is the BEV stock (million vehicles).

**Charging mark-up** on the electricity price falls with the EV share of the passenger stock $e_t$:

$$
mku_t = \max\!\left(0.02,\ 0.3\,\frac{0.5 - e_t}{1 - 0.5}\right)\times 0.2
$$ {#eq-tr-markup}

(minimum and maximum mark-up in USD per kWh, the EV share where the minimum is reached, the share of public charging).
The **EV electricity price** is last year's end-user price plus the mark-up, $p^{EV}_{u,t} = p^{T}_{u,t-1} + mku_t$,
for residential ($u = res$: passenger vehicles, 2-3 wheelers, PHEVs) and industrial users ($u = ind$: freight). Using
last year's price avoids a circular reference with the power model.

**Range anxiety** (USD per vehicle, by class) keeps its start value for the first three years, then falls with the
growth of charging stations:

$$
RA_{k,t} = \begin{cases} RA^{0}_k & t - t_0 + 1 \le 3 \\ RA_{k,t-1} & RA_{k,t-1} < 0 \\ \max\!\left(0,\ RA_{k,t-1}\,(1 - \delta_k)\left(\dfrac{H_t}{H_{t-1}}\right)^{-0.5}\right) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-ra}

where $\delta_k$ is an annual decline (default 0) and $RA^0_k$ the start value from Transport3.

**The start value is fitted.** $RA^0_k$ is the value that makes the model's EV share of purchases in the fit year
(2025, scenario 1) equal the observed share:

$$
r_k(RA^0_k) = s^{EV}_{k}(2025;\ RA^0_k) - s^{EV,data}_{k}(2025) = 0
$$ {#eq-tr-rafit}

The root is found offline by a goal seek on this model and stored by country (negative values allowed, issue I145);
countries without a fitted value use the legacy Transport3 value, and countries without either the Transport3
average. The fit is reported in the rows "EV sales share calculated − actual" of the data years (@sec-tr-results).
For the data edition Public01 the fitted values for Egypt are 64,064 USD (passenger), 469,574 USD (freight) and
1,027 USD (2-3 wheeler). Legacy also allowed a Dashboard source of 10,000 USD for every class (`ra_source`,
`ra_dash`); the model uses the per-country values.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: charging and range anxiety"}
```
for t in years:
    cs_sub = 0 if t < TrCsStartYear else \
             TrCsStartLevel + (TrCsTargetLevel - TrCsStartLevel) * min(1, (t - TrCsStartYear) / max(1, TrCsTargetYear - TrCsStartYear))
    cs_sub *= is_policy_scenario
    port_cost[t] = trcpp[t] * (1 - cs_sub)
    stations[t] = trchs[t] if data_year(t) else \
                  stations[t-1] * (bev_stock[t] / bev_stock[t-1]) ** 0.3 * (port_cost[t] / port_cost[t-1]) ** -0.67
    markup[t] = max(0.02, 0.3 * (0.5 - ev_share_stock[t]) / (1 - 0.5)) * 0.2
    pev[res, t] = rp[res, t-1] + markup[t];  pev[ind, t] = rp[ind, t-1] + markup[t]
    for k in ["pas", "fre", "cyc"]:
        if t - base_year + 1 <= TrRALag:  ra[k, t] = ra_start[k]          # fitted (goal seek)
        elif ra[k, t-1] < 0:              ra[k, t] = ra[k, t-1]
        else: ra[k, t] = max(ra[k, t-1] * (1 - ra_decline[k]) * (stations[t] / stations[t-1]) ** -0.5, 0)
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: charging"}
- **Excel-AI:** Mitigation section 5b: `trcss` (`CSRAMP`), `trcsc`, `trsta` (`STATIONS`), `trmku` (`MARKUP`),
  `trpev` (residential and industrial), `trra` (`RANGEANX`; start values from Transport3 by `CtryName`, the fitted
  values written over the country's Transport3 cells in bright yellow; `IFERROR(..., AVERAGE(RAPas))` fallback).
  Named constant `TrRALag` = 3. Parameters `trp.chs`, `trp.mku`. Fit: `extract/ra_goalseek.py` (scenario 1, 2025),
  stored in `data/<edition>/tidy/range_anxiety_fit.csv`.
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_year()`, block "charging stations, charging mark-up, range anxiety";
  `road_data.range_anxiety` (fitted value, else Transport3, else the Transport3 average).
:::

## Fuel economy of new vehicles and the feebate {#sec-tr-fenew}

New vehicles become more efficient over time, and faster when fuel is dear. A vehicle feebate (a fee on
high-emission vehicles and a rebate on low-emission ones) acts as if it raised the fuel price
([A3.8](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-8)). The methodology describes this efficiency margin of the price response in
[section 3.3.5.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#price-elasticities).

**The feebate rate** (USD per tCO2) is the scenario's vehicle feebate from its introduction year, plus the road
regulation shadow price; it applies in policy scenarios only:

$$
\beta_{k,t} = \pi_t\left(\mathbb{1}[t \ge t^{fb}_k]\,\beta^{0}_k + reg_{rod,t}\right)
$$ {#eq-tr-fbrate}

where $\beta^0_k$ is `TrFbRate<k>`, $t^{fb}_k$ is `TrFbYear<k>` and $reg_{rod,t}$ the road regulation shadow price
(@sec-model-overview). The carbon price is not added: it is in the fuel price already.

**Feebate per liter** is the rate × the fossil CO2 per liter of the fuel:

$$
fb_{k,f,t} = \beta_{k,t}\, \varepsilon_f\, \theta_f
$$ {#eq-tr-fbl}

where $\varepsilon_f$ is the CO2 emission factor (tCO2 per liter) and $\theta_f$ the fossil share of road gasoline
and diesel in the base year (base-year fossil use / (fossil + bioethanol or biodiesel); 1 for LPG and gas).

**New fuel economy** is the data × (1 + gap) in data years, then responds to the price incl. the feebate and gains an
autonomous efficiency improvement:

$$
fe^{new}_{k,f,t} = \begin{cases} fe^{data}_{k,f,t}\,(1 + \gamma_k) & \text{data year} \\ fe^{new}_{k,f,t-1}\left(\dfrac{p_{f,t} + fb_{k,f,t}}{p_{f,t-1} + fb_{k,f,t-1}}\right)^{|\epsilon_{F}|}(1 + \alpha) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-fenew}

where

- $\gamma_k = 0.05$ is how much better new vehicles are than the stock average (`fe_gap`);
- $\epsilon_F$ is the road efficiency elasticity (passenger and 2-3 wheeler: gasoline's for every fuel; freight:
  diesel's);
- $\alpha$ is the autonomous efficiency gain of road oil;
- $p_{f,t}$ is the fuel price (freight: net of VAT; PHEV: the PHEV price, its ratio taken on the average passenger
  price).

The **average new ICEV** fuel economy and CO2 intensity weight the fuels by last year's stock shares (data years: the
vehicle shares); CO2 intensity of a fuel is $\varepsilon_f \cdot 10^6 / fe$ (gCO2 per km). **Used vehicles** carry
the past: their fuel economy is the average new fuel economy of the last $\min(n, t - t_0 + 1)$ years, their CO2
intensity and their BEV fuel economy those of new vehicles $n - 1$ years earlier.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: new fuel economy"}
```
for t in years:
    for k in ["pas", "fre", "cyc"]:
        fb_rate[k, t] = ((TrFbRate[k] if t >= TrFbYear[k] else 0) + reg[rod, t]) * is_policy_scenario
        for f in fuels[k]:
            fb_l[k, f, t] = fb_rate[k, t] * ef[f] * fossil_share[f]
            if data_year(t):
                fe_new[k, f, t] = fe_data[k, f, t] * (1 + fe_gap[k])
            else:
                ratio = (price[f, t] + fb_l[k, f, t]) / (price[f, t-1] + fb_l[k, f, t-1])
                fe_new[k, f, t] = fe_new[k, f, t-1] * ratio ** abs(ela_eff[k]) * (1 + aeei)
            intensity[k, f, t] = ef[f] * 1e6 / fe_new[k, f, t]
        weights = vehicle_share_data if data_year(t) else stock_share[k, :, t-1]
        fe_new_avg[k, t] = weighted_average(fe_new[k, :, t], weights)
    m = min(own_years, t - base_year + 1)
    fe_used[t] = mean(fe_new_avg[pas, t-m+1 : t+1])
    intensity_used[t] = intensity_avg[pas, t-m+1];  fe_used_bev[t] = fe_new_bev[pas, t-m+1]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: new fuel economy"}

  `trfbl` (`FEEBATE`), `trfbr`, `trfbr5`, `trfn`, `trfnp` (`NEWFE`), `trfna`, `trint`, `trinta`, `trfeu`, `trintu`,
  `trfeub`, `tricl`, `triclu`, `trints`; freight `trfewf` ... `trintsf`; 2-3 wheelers `trfblc` ... `trintsc`.
  Parameters `trp.gap`, `trp.ela`, `trp.mod`, `trp.ef`, `trp.efa`.
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_year()`, block "fuel economy of new vehicles and the feebate".

## Distance for the purchase decision {#sec-tr-disttco}

A buyer values a vehicle by the distance they expect to drive it. This distance per new vehicle is the data in data
years, then follows income and, if switched on, the cost per km:

$$
v^{new}_{k,f,t} = v^{new}_{k,f,t-1}\left(\frac{c^{km}_{k,f,t}}{c^{km}_{k,f,t-1}}\right)^{\epsilon_U \cdot \chi}(1 + g_{t-1})^{\eta_k}, \qquad c^{km}_{k,f,t} = \frac{p_{f,t}}{fe^{new}_{k,f,t}} + \tau^{km}_{k,t}
$$ {#eq-tr-vktco}

where

- $c^{km}$ is the cost per km of a new vehicle (BEV: EV electricity price / new BEV fuel economy), USD per km;
- $\tau^{km}_{k,t}$ is the distance tax (@eq-tr-dtax), USD per km;
- $\epsilon_U$ is the road usage elasticity (gasoline for passenger and 2-3 wheelers, diesel for freight);
- $\chi$ is 1 if the TCO distance responds to prices (`vkt_new_price`), 0 by default (legacy Dashboard Q551);
- $g_{t-1}$ is last year's GDP growth and $\eta_k$ the income elasticity of distance.

Freight distance is kept between 50,000 and 120,000 km. Used vehicles drive in proportion to their relative fuel
economy, $v^{used} = \bar{v}^{new}\,(\bar{fe}^{new}/fe^{used})^{\epsilon_U}$ (BEVs likewise with BEV fuel economy).

**The distance tax** (policy scenarios only) starts at its first-year amount and rises linearly to its target, then
stays there:

$$
\tau^{km}_{k,t} = \pi_t\, \mathbb{1}[t \ge t^{dt}_0] \cdot \begin{cases} \tau_0 & t = t^{dt}_0 \\ \min\!\left(\tau_1,\ \tau^{km}_{k,t-1} + \dfrac{\tau_1 - \tau_0}{t^{dt}_1 - t^{dt}_0}\right) & t > t^{dt}_0 \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-dtax}

with `TrDtYear<k>`, `TrDtStart<k>`, `TrDtTargetYear<k>`, `TrDtTarget<k>`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: distance for the TCO"}

  `trckr`, `trvkn` (`GROWVKT`), `trvkna`, `trckbp`, `trckbr`, `trckbf`, `trckbc`, `trvknb`, `trvku`, `trvkub`
  (`USEDVKT`), `trckf`, `trckfr`, `trvknf`, `trvknaf`, `trvknbf` (`CLAMPVKT`), `trckc`, `trckcr`, `trvkncg`,
  `trvkncb`. The price-response switch is a 0/1 parameter (`trp.vkt` G).

## Total cost of ownership {#sec-tr-tco}

The choice between an ICEV and a BEV is made on the total cost of ownership per km: what the vehicle costs to buy,
insure, maintain and fuel over the years it is owned, discounted, divided by the discounted distance it is driven
([A3.7](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-7)).

### Discounted distance and purchase price {#sec-tr-price}

**Discounted distance** over the ownership period is the present value of the yearly distance:

$$
K_{k,v,t} = v_{k,v,t}\,\frac{(1 + r_t)^{N_k} - 1}{r_t\,(1 + r_t)^{N_k}}
$$ {#eq-tr-dkm}

with $N_{pas} = 7$, $N_{pau} = 13$, $N_{fre} = 10$, $N_{cyc} = 7$ and $r_t$ the consumer discount rate
(@eq-tr-disc).

**Purchase price after policies.** For an ICEV and a BEV of class $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P^{ICE}_{k,t} &= P^{0,ICE}_{k,t}\,(1 + du^{ICE}_k\, m_k)(1 + adv^{ICE}_{k,t})(1 + vat_k) + FB^{ICE}_{k,t} \\
P^{BEV}_{k,t} &= P^{0,BEV}_{k,t}\,(1 + du^{BEV}_{k,t}\, m_k)(1 + vat^{BEV}_{k,t})(1 + adv^{BEV}_{k,t}) + FB^{BEV}_{k,t} + sub_{k,t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-tr-price}

where

- $P^{0}$ is the vehicle price before taxes (Transport2), USD;
- $du_k$ the import duty and $m_k$ the share of imports (customs and import data years);
- $adv$ the ad-valorem purchase tax: the baseline rate, or the policy rate from `TrAdvYear<k>` in policy scenarios
  (`TrAdvIceBase`, `TrAdvBevBase`, `TrAdvIcePol`, `TrAdvBevPol`);
- $vat_k$ the VAT on vehicles (0 for freight); for BEVs the policy rate (baseline × `TrVatPolFactor`) applies from
  `TrVatYear<k>`, and the policy BEV duty (baseline × `TrCustPolFactor`) from `TrCustYear<k>`;
- $FB$ the vehicle feebate (@eq-tr-fbveh);
- $sub_{k,t}$ the EV purchase subsidy (negative), @eq-tr-sub.

**The vehicle feebate** charges the CO2 intensity above a pivot, at the feebate rate, over the discounted distance:

$$
FB^{v}_{k,t} = \left(I^{v}_{k,t} - I^{piv}_{k,t}\right)\frac{\beta_{k,t}}{10^6}\, K_{k,v,t}
$$ {#eq-tr-fbveh}

where $I^{v}$ is the CO2 intensity of the vehicle (gCO2 per km; BEVs 0; used ICEVs the used intensity) and $I^{piv}$
the pivot. Below the pivot the feebate is a rebate. The pivot is blank in the first two years, then either

- **Average:** last year's sales-weighted intensity extrapolated by its own trend,
  $I^{piv}_t = \bar{I}_{t}\,\bar{I}_{t}/\bar{I}_{t-1}$, where $\bar{I}_t$ is the intensity of last year's sales
  (new and used, weighted by their ICE shares); or
- **Manual:** `TrFbPivot<k>` in the feebate year, then lower by `TrFbPivotChg<k>` gCO2 per km each year, at least 0
  (0 before the feebate year).

The **EV subsidy** (policy scenarios only) is $-$`TrSubAmount<k>` in its year, then changes by `TrSubChg<k>` a year,
never positive:

$$
sub_{k,t} = \pi_t \cdot \begin{cases} -A_k & t = t^{sub}_k \\ \min(0,\ sub_{k,t-1} - \Delta_k) & t > t^{sub}_k \\ 0 & t < t^{sub}_k \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-tr-sub}

### Cost components {#sec-tr-costs}

The TCO of a new vehicle adds five parts. With $P$ the price after policies, $d = 0.30$ the first-year depreciation,
$L$ the useful life, $n$ the ownership period and $r$ the discount rate:

$$
\begin{aligned}
D^{1} &= d\,P && \text{first-year depreciation} \\
D^{ann} &= \frac{P - dP}{L - 1}\cdot\frac{1 - (1 + r)^{-(L-1)}}{r} && \text{depreciation annuity of the rest} \\
SV &= \min\!\left(0,\ -P\,\frac{(L - n)/L\,(1 - d)}{(1 + r)^{n}}\right) && \text{salvage value (passenger only)} \\
IM &= \frac{P\,\iota}{r}\left(1 - (1 + r)^{-(n+1)}\right)\theta + m^{v}\,K && \text{insurance and maintenance} \\
FU &= \left(\frac{p}{fe^{new}} + \tau^{km}\right)K && \text{fuel or electricity and distance tax}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-tr-parts}

where $\iota = 1.5\%$ is the insurance rate, $\theta = 0.5$ the insurance factor, $m^{v}$ the maintenance cost per km
(ICEV or EV), $p$ the average ICE fuel price over the fuel mix and $fe^{new}$ the average new fuel economy (BEVs: the
EV electricity price and new BEV fuel economy). Then

$$
TCO^{v}_{k,t} = D^1 + D^{ann} + SV + IM + FU + \mathbb{1}[v = BEV]\,RA_{k,t}, \qquad c^{v}_{k,t} = \frac{TCO^{v}_{k,t}}{K_{k,v,t}}
$$ {#eq-tr-tco}

**Used passenger vehicles** are bought at their resale price after taxes,
$P^{res} = P^{0}\left(1 - \big(d + \frac{n - 1}{L - 1}(1 - d)\big)\right) \times$ (the same tax factors) + the feebate
(BEV: + the subsidy). Their TCO has no first-year depreciation and no salvage value: the annuity is over the used
ownership period less one year, $13 - 1 = 12$ years, for ICEVs and BEVs alike; insurance runs over 13 years; fuel uses
the used fuel economy. A used BEV carries range anxiety scaled by its price, $RA^{used} = RA\,P^{used}/P^{new}$.

**Freight vehicles and 2-3 wheelers** have no salvage term; freight pays no VAT and charges at the industrial EV
price, 2-3 wheelers at the residential one.

**Per-fuel ICE TCO** (for the fuel split of @sec-tr-choice) uses the cost per km of each fuel and shares the feebate
by intensity:
$TCO_f = K\,c^{km}_f + (D^1 + D^{ann} + SV) + IM + FB\,(I_f/\bar{I})$.

**Plug-in hybrids** take the BEV's capital cost (no PHEV price exists in the data): BEV depreciation and salvage,
insurance on the BEV price, ICEV maintenance over the ICEV distance, and the PHEV fuel cost; they carry **no range
anxiety**, since they refuel with gasoline.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: TCO of a new passenger ICEV and BEV"}
```
for t in years:
    r = disc[t]
    K_ice = v_new_avg * ((1 + r) ** own_years - 1) / (r * (1 + r) ** own_years)
    K_bev = v_new_bev * ((1 + r) ** own_years - 1) / (r * (1 + r) ** own_years)
    fb_ice = (intensity_avg[t] - pivot[t]) * fb_rate[t] / 1e6 * K_ice      # blank in the base year
    fb_bev = (0 - pivot[t]) * fb_rate[t] / 1e6 * K_bev
    P_ice = price0_ice[t] * (1 + duty_ice * imp) * (1 + adv_ice[t]) * (1 + vat) + fb_ice
    P_bev = price0_bev[t] * (1 + cust_bev[t]) * (1 + vat_bev[t]) * (1 + adv_bev[t]) + subsidy[t] + fb_bev
    for v, P, K, maint, fuel_km in [("ice", P_ice, K_ice, maint_ice, p_avg / fe_new_avg + dtax),
                                    ("bev", P_bev, K_bev, maint_ev, pev[res] / fe_new_bev + dtax)]:
        dep1 = dep * P
        ann = (P - dep1) / (life - 1) / r * (1 - (1 + r) ** -(life - 1))
        salv = min(0, -P * ((life - own_years) / life * (1 - dep)) / (1 + r) ** own_years)
        ins_m = P * ins / r * (1 - (1 + r) ** -(own_years + 1)) * ins_factor + maint * K
        tco[v] = dep1 + ann + salv + ins_m + fuel_km * K + (ra[pas, t] if v == "bev" else 0)
        tco_km[v] = tco[v] / K
```
:::

## Choice: the EV share and the ICE fuel split {#sec-tr-choice}

Buyers choose between an ICEV and a BEV by their TCO per km. The model uses a binary logit, as the power model does
for dispatch and investment (methodology
[section 3.4.2.4.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#logit-function)); among ICEVs, the fuel mix
shifts with the relative TCO of each fuel ([M5.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M5-2),
[A3.7](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-7)).

**EV share of purchases.** For each class (new passenger, used passenger, freight, 2-3 wheelers):

$$
s^{ICE}_{k,t} = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\left(-k_k\,\dfrac{c^{BEV}_{k,t} - c^{ICE}_{k,t}}{\bar{c}_{k,t}}\right)}, \qquad s^{BEV}_{k,t} = 1 - s^{ICE}_{k,t}, \qquad \bar{c}_{k,t} = s^{ICE}_{k,t-1}\,c^{ICE}_{k,t} + (1 - s^{ICE}_{k,t-1})\,c^{BEV}_{k,t}
$$ {#eq-tr-logit}

where $k_k$ is the logit parameter (3 passenger, 2 freight, 4 2-3 wheelers) and $\bar{c}$ the average TCO per km
weighted by last year's ICE share (base year: 1 − the data EV share). This is the two-option form of the equation
list's multinomial logit. In data years the actual shares replace the logit. The passenger EV share of purchases is
$u\,s^{BEV}_{pau} + (1 - u)\,s^{BEV}_{pas}$, the actual share where there is one.

**ICE fuel split of passenger purchases.** In data years the shares are the base-year distance split scaled to the ICE
total; the PHEV share is (EV − BEV purchase share) × the passenger share $\sigma$, at least 0. Afterwards each fuel's
share moves with its own TCO change and the TCO change of the other fuels:

$$
\tilde{s}_{f,t} = \tilde{s}_{f,t-1}\left(\frac{TCO_{f,t}}{TCO_{f,t-1}}\right)^{-1.265}\left(\frac{\sum_{g \ne f}\tilde{s}_{g,t-1}\,TCO_{g,t}/TCO_{g,t-1}}{\sum_{g \ne f}\tilde{s}_{g,t-1}}\right)^{0.5725}
$$ {#eq-tr-icesplit}

over $f, g \in$ {gasoline, diesel, LPG, CNG, PHEV}. If no other fuel has a share the share is held. The shares are
then scaled to the ICE part of purchases, $s_{f,t} = \tilde{s}_{f,t} / \sum_g \tilde{s}_{g,t}\,(1 - s^{EV}_t)$.

**Stock shares** turn over slowly: each year the ownership period's share of the stock is replaced,

$$
s^{stock}_{f,t} = s^{stock}_{f,t-1}\,\frac{Y - 1}{Y} + \frac{s_{f,t}}{Y}
$$ {#eq-tr-stockshare}

with $Y$ the ownership years ($u\,L_{pas} + (1-u)\,n$; 13.57 for Egypt) for passenger vehicles and $L_{fre} = 10$ for
freight; data years take the data. Divided by their sum plus the EV stock share, they give the vehicles by fuel
(million) = passenger stock × share × population / 1,000.

Freight follows the same steps with diesel, LPG and LNG, scaled to $1 - s^{BEV}_{fre}$. 2-3 wheelers have only
gasoline ICEVs.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: EV choice and ICE fuel split"}
```
for t in years:
    for k in ["pas", "pau", "fre", "cyc"]:
        avg = ice_share[k, t-1] * tco_km[k, ice] + (1 - ice_share[k, t-1]) * tco_km[k, bev]
        logit_ice = 1 / (1 + exp(-k_par[k] * (tco_km[k, bev] - tco_km[k, ice]) / avg))
        ice_share[k, t] = 1 - ev_share_data[k, t] if data_year(t) else logit_ice
    for f in ["gso", "die", "lpg", "nga", "phv"]:
        if data_year(t):
            s[f, t] = data_split[f, t]
        else:
            ratio = tco_f[f, t] / tco_f[f, t-1]
            others = [g for g in fuels if g != f]
            cross = sum(s[g, t-1] * tco_f[g, t] / tco_f[g, t-1] for g in others) / sum(s[g, t-1] for g in others)
            s[f, t] = s[f, t-1] * ratio ** own_price_el * cross ** cross_price_el
    for f: s_new[f, t] = s[f, t] if data_year(t) else s[f, t] / sum(s[:, t]) * (1 - ev_share[pas, t])
    for f: s_stock[f, t] = data if data_year(t) else s_stock[f, t-1] * (Y - 1) / Y + s_new[f, t] / Y
```
:::

  (`ACTSHARE`), `trshn`, `trshnb`, `trtcau`, `trlgu`, `trlgub`, `trshu`, `trshub`, `trevcc`, `trevsh` (`ACTORCALC`),
  `trtrn`, `trnwbn`, `trnwbu`; ICE split `trics`, `trtcr`, `tricd`, `tricdp`, `trcrs` (`CROSSRATIO`; IFERROR for
  "other fuels without share"), `tricp` (`ICESPLIT`), `tricn` (`NORMSH`), `trico` (`OWNSH`), `tricw`, `trveh`,
  `trvehb`; freight `trtcaf` ... `trvehfb`; 2-3 wheelers `trtcac` ... `trvehc`.
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_year()`, block "EV choice", and `_ice_shares()`.

## Stock fuel economy, distance driven and fuel use {#sec-tr-fuel}

Fuel use is vehicles × distance per vehicle / fuel economy of the stock
([M5.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M5-3), [A3.8](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-8)). Each factor is projected separately.

**Stock fuel economy** turns over with the purchases: the data in data years, then

$$
fe^{stock}_{k,f,t} = \tau_k\, fe^{new}_{k,f,t} + (1 - \tau_k)\, fe^{stock}_{k,f,t-1}
$$ {#eq-tr-festock}

with the turnover share $\tau_{pas} = 1/\big(u\,n + (1-u)\,L_{pas}\big)$ (7 years used, 20 new), $\tau_{fre} = 1/10$,
$\tau_{cyc} = 1/7$. The opening value is last year's closing value. The BEV stock fuel economy turns over in the same
way, with the share of this year's BEV purchases in the closing BEV stock and the new BEV fuel economy (passenger: new
and used BEVs weighted by their purchases).

**Distance per vehicle** is the data in data years (times the calibration factor of @eq-tr-distfactor), then responds
to the cost per km of the stock and to income:

$$
v_{k,f,t} = v_{k,f,t-1}\left(\frac{c^{stock}_{k,f,t}}{c^{stock}_{k,f,t-1}}\right)^{\epsilon_U}\left(\frac{y_t}{y_{t-1}}\right)^{\eta_k}, \qquad c^{stock}_{k,f,t} = \frac{p_{f,t}}{fe^{stock,o}_{k,f,t}} + \tau^{km}_{k,t}
$$ {#eq-tr-vkt}

where $fe^{stock,o}$ is the opening stock fuel economy, $\epsilon_U$ the usage elasticity and $\eta_k$ the income
elasticity of distance (2-3 wheelers: −0.4, so they are driven less as income rises). The base distance is the
Transport1 average distance (passenger and light blended; freight from the fuel shares, @sec-tr-datayears; BEVs with
their uplift).

**Distance driven and fuel use:**

$$
B_{k,f,t} = \frac{V_{k,f,t}\, v_{k,f,t}}{1000}, \qquad F_{k,f,t} = \frac{B_{k,f,t}}{fe^{stock}_{k,f,t}}
$$ {#eq-tr-fueluse}

where $V$ is vehicles (million), $B$ billion km and $F$ billion liters (BEVs: billion kWh). Here $fe$ is km per
liter, so the equation list's $F = \sum VKT \cdot FE$ ([M5.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M5-3)) reads with $FE = 1/fe$.
PHEV distance is split: gasoline use $B_{phv}/fe_{phv}$ is added to gasoline, electricity use is
$B_{phv}(1 - \phi)/fe^{BEV}$. CO2 by class is fuel use × the emission factor.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: fuel use by class"}
```
for t in years:
    for k, f in classes_and_fuels:
        fe_open[k, f, t] = fe_data[k, f, t] if data_year(t) else fe_stock[k, f, t-1]
        fe_stock[k, f, t] = fe_data[k, f, t] if data_year(t) else \
                            turnover[k] * fe_new[k, f, t] + (1 - turnover[k]) * fe_open[k, f, t]
        cost_km[k, f, t] = price[f, t] / fe_open[k, f, t] + dtax[k, t]
        if data_year(t):
            v[k, f, t] = v_data[k, t] * dist_factor[k]
        else:
            v[k, f, t] = v[k, f, t-1] * (cost_km[k, f, t] / cost_km[k, f, t-1]) ** ela_usage[k] \
                         * (gpc[t] / gpc[t-1]) ** inc_el[k]
        bkm[k, f, t] = vehicles[k, f, t] * v[k, f, t] / 1000           # billion km
        fuel[k, f, t] = bkm[k, f, t] / fe_stock[k, f, t]               # billion liters
    fuel[pas, gso, t] += bkm[pas, phv, t] / fe_stock[pas, phv, t]
    elec[pas, t] = bkm[pas, bev, t] / fe_bev_stock[t] + bkm[pas, phv, t] / fe_bev_stock[t] * (1 - phev_gso_share)
```
:::

  (`OPENFE`, `STOCKFE`), `trcks`, `trcksr`, `trgpcr`, `trvku0`, `trbkm0`, `trfu0g`, `trfu0` (`VKTFUEL`,
  `TWOFUEL`), freight `trfsof` ... `trfu0f`, 2-3 wheelers `trfsoc` ... `trfu0c`; calibrated `trvkc`, `trbkm`,
  `trfup`, `trco2p` (`EMITFUEL`), `trfebn` (`BEVFENEW`), `trfebo` (`BEVFEOPEN`), `trfebs`, `trckb2`, `trckb2r`,
  `trvkcb`, `trbkmb`, `trelph` (`PHEVELE`), `trelp`, `trbkmt`, `trintp` (`INTENSITY`); freight `trvkcf` ...
  `trintf2` (`INTENS0`); 2-3 wheelers `trvkcc` ... `trintc2`.

## Calibration to the energy balance {#sec-tr-calibration}

The bottom-up fleet (Transport1 ownership × distance / fuel economy) rarely adds up to the road fuel use of the energy
balance. Two calibration steps close the gap in the base year; their factors are then held
([A3.8](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-8), [A3.9](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-9)).

**Step 1: distance factors by class.** The bottom-up base-year fuel use, grossed up for buses, is compared with the
energy balance fuel by fuel:

$$
Q^{bu}_{f} = \frac{F^{0}_{f,t_0}\, 10^9 / \lambda_f}{1 - b_f}, \qquad q_f = \frac{F^{bal}_{f,t_0}}{Q^{bu}_f}
$$ {#eq-tr-cq}

where $F^{0}_{f,t_0}$ is uncalibrated fuel use (billion liters: gasoline = passenger + 2-3 wheelers; diesel, LPG and gas
= passenger + freight), $b_f$ the bus share of the fuel (gasoline 0), and $q_f = 1$ when either is zero. The distance
factor of a class is the fuel-use-weighted average of the $q_f$:

$$
\kappa_{pas} = \frac{\sum_f F^{0}_{pas,f}\, q_f}{\sum_f F^{0}_{pas,f}}, \qquad \kappa_{fre} = \frac{\sum_f F^{0}_{fre,f}\, q_f}{\sum_f F^{0}_{fre,f}}, \qquad \kappa_{cyc} = q_{gso}
$$ {#eq-tr-distfactor}

The factors multiply the data distance of each class in @eq-tr-vkt (BEVs too) and are held after the base year.

**Step 2: a residual factor by fuel.** After buses (@sec-tr-buses) the calibrated total still differs from the energy
balance, because a class factor averages over fuels. A second factor by fuel closes it:

$$
\gamma_f = \frac{F^{bal}_{f,t_0}}{F_{f,t_0}\,10^9/\lambda_f}, \qquad F^{T}_{f,t} = F_{f,t}\,\frac{10^9}{\lambda_f}\,\gamma_f
$$ {#eq-tr-ktoe}

where $F_{f,t}$ is road use of the fuel (billion liters: gasoline = passenger + 2-3 wheelers; diesel, LPG and gas =
passenger + freight + buses) and $F^{T}_{f,t}$ the result in ktoe. In the base year $F^{T}$ equals the energy balance.
Electricity has a factor only if `recon_ele` = Yes (default No, factor 1):

$$
E^{T}_t = E_t\,\frac{1000}{\omega}\,\gamma_{e}
$$ {#eq-tr-ktoe-el}

with $E_t$ road electricity (billion kWh: buses, 2-3 wheelers, freight, passenger), $\omega$ GWh per ktoe.

The factors are large where the data explain little of road fuel use: for Egypt, passenger distance × 2.67 (freight
1.70, 2-3 wheelers 3.30), then gasoline × 1.23 (diesel 0.86, gas 1.14). The workbook reports them.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: calibration"}
```
if t == base_year:
    for f in ["gso", "die", "lpg", "nga"]:
        liters = fuel0[pas, gso] + fuel0[cyc, gso] if f == "gso" else fuel0[pas, f] + fuel0[fre, f]
        bottom_up[f] = liters / liters_per_ktoe[f] * 1e9 / (1 - bus_share[f])
        q[f] = 1 if bottom_up[f] == 0 or eb[f] == 0 else eb[f] / bottom_up[f]
    dist_factor[pas] = sum(fuel0[pas, f] * q[f]) / sum(fuel0[pas, f])
    dist_factor[fre] = sum(fuel0[fre, f] * q[f]) / sum(fuel0[fre, f])
    dist_factor[cyc] = q["gso"]
    # ... calibrated fuel use and buses ...
    for f: cf2[f] = 1 if road_liters[f] == 0 or eb[f] == 0 else eb[f] / (road_liters[f] / liters_per_ktoe[f] * 1e9)
    cf2[ecy] = 1 if recon_ele == "No" or elec == 0 or eb[ecy] == 0 else eb[ecy] / (elec / gwh_per_ktoe * 1000)
# held after the base year
trkt[f, t] = road_liters[f, t] / liters_per_ktoe[f] * 1e9 * cf2[f]
trkte[t] = elec[t] * 1000 / gwh_per_ktoe * cf2[ecy]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: calibration"}
- **Excel-AI:** Mitigation section 5b: step 1 `trbu`, `trcq`, `trdfp`, `trdff`, `trdfc` (`HOLD`); step 2 `trcf2`,
  `trcf2e`; results `trkt` (`KTOE`), `trkte` (`KTOEELE`).
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_fuel_use()`, blocks "calibration of distance" and "totals, the calibration to the
  energy balance".
:::

## Buses {#sec-tr-buses}

Buses are not modelled as a fleet. Their base-year fuel use (from the Transport1 fuel shares) moves with passenger
energy use:

$$
F_{bus,f,t} = F_{bus,f,t_0}\,\frac{\sum_g F^{kt}_{pas,g,t}}{U_{t_0}}, \qquad E_{bus,t} = \Big(\sum_f F^{kt}_{bus,f,t_0} + E^{kt}_{bus,t_0}\Big)\frac{E^{kt}_{pas,t}}{U_{t_0}}
$$ {#eq-tr-bus}

where

- $F_{bus,f,t_0}$ is base-year bus use of diesel, LPG and gas (billion liters);
- $F^{kt}_{pas,g,t}$ is passenger fuel use in ktoe and $E^{kt}_{pas,t}$ passenger electricity in ktoe;
- $U_{t_0}$ is base-year passenger fuel and electricity use (ktoe, held);
- $E^{kt}_{bus,t_0}$ is base-year bus electricity: the passenger EV stock share of 2024 × base-year bus fuel.

Bus electricity is converted to billion kWh. All base-year bus energy electrifies with passenger electricity, as
legacy.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: buses"}
- **Excel-AI:** Mitigation section 5b, buses: `trbusp`, `trbuse`, `trbus0`, `trbusf` (`BUSFUEL`), `trbusel`
  (`BUSELE`); parameter `trp.bus`.
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_fuel_use()`, block "buses".
:::

## Results and links to the rest of the model {#sec-tr-results}

The engineer model delivers road fuel and electricity use in ktoe, and a set of fleet indicators
([A3.9](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A3-9)).

**Road biofuels** follow the engineer gasoline and diesel: bioethanol and other biofuels with gasoline, biodiesel with
diesel, as legacy:

$$
F^{T}_{bio,t} = \big(F^{bal}_{bgs,t_0} + F^{bal}_{obf,t_0}\big)\frac{F^{T}_{gso,t}}{F^{bal}_{gso,t_0}} + F^{bal}_{bdi,t_0}\,\frac{F^{T}_{die,t}}{F^{bal}_{die,t_0}}
$$ {#eq-tr-bio}

(base-year value held where base-year gasoline or diesel is zero). Base-year biofuels come from Balances or EnergyCons
(`BalancesOrConsumption`). Under the elasticity model road biofuels follow the elasticity gasoline and diesel instead
(@sec-demand).

| Result | Unit | Code | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Road gasoline, diesel, LPG, gas | ktoe | `trkt` | Fuel use when switched on (@eq-tr-fuelswitch) |
| Road biofuels | ktoe | `trbio` | Fuel use when switched on |
| Road electricity | ktoe | `trkte` | Power demand when switched on, from the year after the base year (@eq-tr-elswitch) |
| Road fuel and electricity use, total | ktoe | `trsum` | Summary row |
| Distance driven by class, total | billion km | `trkmp`, `trkmf`, `trkmc`, `trkmt` | Indicator (× the gasoline factor for passenger and 2-3 wheelers, the diesel factor for freight) |
| Fuel and electricity use by class (calibrated) | billion liters, billion kWh | `trfcp`, `trfcf`, `trfcc`, `trfcep`, `trfcef`, `trfcec` | Indicator |
| Average fuel economy: gasoline; diesel, LPG, gas; EVs | km per liter, km per kWh | `trafg`, `trafo`, `trafe` | Indicator (weighted by fuel use; fixed weights `TrFEW*` when there is no use) |
| Vehicles by class, total | million | `trvht`, `trvhtf`, `trvhtc`, `trvhta` | Indicator |
| EV sales share, calculated − actual (data years) | share | `trrafp`, `trraff`, `trrafc` | Range-anxiety fit (@eq-tr-rafit) |
| Road and total fuel use of the switched model; road share | ktoe; share | `trq`, `tran.rsh` | Transport co-benefits module (@sec-fiscal) |

The **transport co-benefits module** (accidents, congestion, road damage; methodology
[section 3.7.1.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#co-benefits) and
[section 7.7.5](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/07_Road_Transport.html#sec-extcost)) reads road fuel use of whichever
model is switched on (`ener`, electricity `eldem`) and its share of total use.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: results"}
- **Excel-AI:** Mitigation section 5b ("5b. Road transport: engineer model and outputs to the transport co-benefits
  module"): `trfua`, `trfub`, `trelt`, `trcf2`, `trcf2e`, `trkt`, `trbio` (road biofuels), `trkte`, `trkmp` ...
  `trkmt`, `trfcp` ... `trfcc`, `trafg`, `trafo` (`AVGFE`), `trafen` (helper row), `trafe` (`AVGFEEV`), `trvht` ...
  `trvhta`, `trrafp`, `trraff`, `trrafc`, `trq`, `tran.rsh`; summary row `trsum` (visible when the section is rolled
  up). Named constants `TrFEWGso`, `TrFEWHalf`, `TrFEWEvP`, `TrFEWEvO` (fixed weights of the average fuel economy
  without fuel use).
- **CPAT Python:** `road.py`, `_fuel_use()` (totals) and `_results()`.
:::

## Caveats {#sec-tr-caveats}

- **The engineer model is off by default.** It is a calibration that has not been reviewed for every country; results
  are the elasticity model's unless a scenario sets `TrModel` = Engineer.
- **CPAT Python** computes the engineer model for the co-benefits module but cannot yet run with it switched on.
- **Calibration factors are large** where Transport1 explains only part of road fuel use (for Egypt 30-60%:
  passenger distance × 2.67, then gasoline × 1.23). Review the data before using the engineer results.
- **Range anxiety** is fitted to one year (2025) of observed EV sales in scenario 1; it is the main lever on the EV
  share and absorbs whatever the TCO misses.
- **Freight distance** in the TCO is the Transport1 average (Egypt 48,630 km), floored at 50,000 km, which binds in
  every projection year; fuel use uses the distance derived from fuel shares (Egypt 8,091 km × 1.70). Kept as legacy
  (open question B14, @sec-tr-open).
- **Data years of inputs** are kept as legacy: VAT on vehicles and customs duties of 2024, import shares of 2022, bus
  electricity from the 2024 EV share.
- **The ownership decline limit** of 10% a year is a placeholder.
- **Not built:** mode shift, and the road externalities of legacy sheet `Transport` driven by the engineer model's
  distance and fuel economy (the co-benefits module works from fuel use instead).
- **Parameters** are legacy values; the methodology note proposes others (@sec-tr-params).

## Comparison with legacy CPAT {#sec-tr-legacy}

The rule is to match legacy CPAT except where legacy has a bug; every difference is listed here. Where a choice was
needed, the recommendation of the transport plan or of the open questions was taken (user decisions of 2026-10-14).

**Sources.** Legacy `CPAT 1.0pre_456_NoPropData.xlsb`: Mitigation key inputs 15 (rows 2015-2171), section 5 (rows
4302-5378; policy copy at +6331), sheets Transport1-3, Dashboard, Manual inputs; the methodology note
`Transportation_methodology.docx`; the map of legacy in `Transport_Legacy_Survey.md`.

**Legacy match.** A Python reference engine (`transport_model_ref.py`) reproduces the cached legacy engineer run with
every fix off, and the workbook is checked against the same engine with every fix on.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: the reference reproduces legacy"}
`legacy_test(run)` drives the engine from the cached legacy inputs with no fix and compares every cached numeric row
4334-5378, the key-input rows 2034-2171 (934 year rows) and 157 side-table scalars, 2022-2041 (relative difference to
max(1e-6, |legacy|)).

| Run | Series compared | Max relative difference | Where |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Baseline (C2173 = 1) | 1,091 | 3.8e-14 | r5222 (PHEV electricity), 2037 |
| Carbon tax (C8504 = 2) | 1,091 | 1.6e-14 | r4817 (used BEV choice), 2025 |

No residual: the differences are floating-point rounding. The legacy range-anxiety start values equal the cached
N4354:N4356 exactly.
:::

### Scope {#sec-tr-scope}

| Topic | Legacy | This model |
|---|---|---|
| Model choice | Switch `TrModel` (MTInputs F340, from the Dashboard): Engineer or Elasticity; the Egypt run uses Elasticity | Same switch, default Elasticity; the engineer model is computed in every run and replaces road gasoline, diesel, LPG, gas and biofuels (and road electricity in power demand) when switched on |
| Coverage | Road only: passenger and light (new and used), freight, 2-3 wheelers, buses (scaled); coal, kerosene and other oil products in road, rail, aviation and navigation by elasticities | Same |
| Externalities | Sheet `Transport` (accidents, congestion, road damage) reads the engineer distance and fuel economy even under Elasticity (survey B16) | Not built; the co-benefits module reads fuel use |
| Mode shift | None | None |

### Decisions relative to legacy {#sec-tr-decisions}

| Topic | Legacy | This model | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default model | Template default Engineer; Egypt run Elasticity | Elasticity by default, Engineer by switch | Results unchanged until the engineer run is reviewed; a calibration that is not general stays off by default |
| Bugs | As found | All fixed (@sec-tr-bugs); legacy behaviour kept as switches in the Python reference only | Same approach as the power model; the reference reproduces legacy to 4e-14 with the switches off |
| Parameters | Side-table and Dashboard values; the methodology note differs | Legacy values; the note's values stored as alternatives (use = note) | Match legacy; switch after review |
| Range anxiety | Transport3: stored per-country solver results from another vintage | Fitted by goal seek on this model (scenario 1, 2025), stored per country; the fit is reported | The stored values did not fit the corrected model (legacy 0.35%, all fixes 0.09%, actual 0.15% for Egypt passenger, before the refit) |
| Calibration to the energy balance | Step 1 distance factors by class; step 2 residual factor by fuel | Same, live formulas; factors reported | General (from data); large factors flag data problems |
| Used vehicle depreciation (B20) | Used ICEV annuity over 6 years, used BEV over 12 | 12 years for both (used ownership period − 1) | User confirmation 2026-10-14 |
| Ownership decline (B4) | Passenger and freight ownership cannot fall | May fall by up to 10% a year (the legacy 2-3 wheeler value) | Placeholder; no effect for Egypt |
| PHEV range anxiety (B23) | PHEV TCO carries the full BEV range anxiety (about 100,000 USD) | None for PHEVs | PHEVs refuel with gasoline; user decision 2026-10-14 |
| Freight distance (survey B14) | TCO uses Transport1 average freight distance (48,630 km, floored at 50,000 km, binding every year); fuel use the derived 8,091 km × calibration | Kept as legacy | Needs a data decision; not a clear bug |
| Data years of inputs | VAT on vehicles and customs from 2024, import shares 2022, bus electricity 2024 | Kept as legacy (parameters) | Legacy input choices, not bugs |
| Policy inputs | Dashboard rows 61-98, 540-558 (outside MTInputs) | ScenarioDefinition rows (scenario-specific, run by the batch macro) | Scenarios must carry the transport policies |
| Hardcoded literals | Gompertz −5.897, gas /26, PHEV × 9, insurance × 0.5, station life /15, BEV distance caps, own and cross price elasticities, BEV fuel-economy and charging-cost paths | Named parameters and data, same values | No literal in a formula |
| Inputs from the rest of the model (LD61) | 2-3 wheeler gasoline price before new policies (row 4438); VAT on vehicles from N726 (Egypt 0.1531) | 2-3 wheelers at the road gasoline price incl. new policies, as passenger (so carbon pricing reaches them); VAT_WEO of the customs year (Egypt 0.14) | Consistency; one VAT source |
| Industrial gas for LNG trucks | Legacy industrial price block | Industrial price + the road new policies | Policies reach LNG trucks |
| Vehicle feebate rate (M13) | Feebate + carbon price × road feebate coverage | Feebate + road regulation shadow price | The carbon price is in the fuel price already |
| Biofuels (LD62) | Engineer: bioethanol and other biofuels with gasoline, biodiesel with diesel; the feebate CO2 per liter × the fossil share (E2146:E2147, issue I40) | Same | Match legacy |

### Legacy bugs fixed {#sec-tr-bugs}

Seventeen legacy bugs of the engineer road model are fixed, plus three of an earlier prototype version. Each legacy
fix is a switch of the Python reference (`FIXES`; `ALL_FIXES` is the corrected model). The B codes follow the survey
of legacy (B1-B17) and continue for bugs found while building the reference (B19-B23); the L codes are those of the
bug register.

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: the bugs fixed"}
| Register | Survey | Legacy rows | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L25 | B1 | 4451, 4720 | Passenger distance tax and 2-3 wheeler EV subsidy test `$C2227>1`; the text "res" > 1 is TRUE, so they apply in the baseline too | Scenario number > 1 |
| L26 | B2 | 4487 AB:AE, 4501 | Freight and 2-3 wheeler income growth read row 2455 (coal producer subsidies) from 2038 | Lagged GDP growth (row 2446) in all years |
| L27 | B3 | H:J4787, H:J4903 | Ownership calibration MAX(1, actual/expected) at 2024 (column N): scales up only | Actual/expected both ways at the last data year in the data (2025) |
| L28 | B3b | $N2168, J2169 | Freight-share cap and 2-3 wheeler peak read 2024 | Last data year |
| L29 | B4 | T4328, U4328 | Passenger and freight ownership cannot fall (maximum decrease 0) | Decrease of up to 10% a year (the legacy 2-3 wheeler value) |
| L30 | B6 | 5310-5314, 5318 | Bus fuel scaled by the wrong rows (LPG, gas and PHEV distance, BEV vehicles); bus electricity from a sum of liters and kWh | Passenger fuel use in ktoe and passenger electricity; base bus energy in ktoe |
| L31 | B6b | O5171:O5173 | Bus share added as × (1 + share) | / (1 − share) |
| L32 | B7 | G4376-G4378, G4419-G4421 | Stale emission-factor names: diesel and LPG use industry EFs, CNG/LNG the residential gas EF | Road EFs |
| L33 | B8 | M5261, M5295, M5232, M4646 | BEV freight distance with the 2-3 wheeler income elasticity; BEV 2-3 wheeler distance with the cost ratio twice and no income term; LPG freight base row; freight ICE depreciation switching to the passenger discount rate from 2023 | As the sibling rows |
| L34 | B8w | K4329 | Freight discounted at the average power-sector WACC | The consumer discount rate (row 4531) |
| L35 | B9 | 4850 L:O | PHEV sales share = passenger EV share − blended passenger/light BEV share (negative) | (EV − BEV passenger share) × passenger share; ICE shares scaled to the rest |
| L36 | B10 | 4343 | Charging-station subsidy ramp accumulates before the start year and is not capped at the target year | 0 before the start year, linear to the target level, then constant |
| L37 | B19 | 4573 | New BEV maintenance at the ICEV rate (J4327) | EV maintenance (J4328) |
| L38 | B20 | 4598 | Used ICEV depreciation annuity over own_years − 1 (6) years, used BEV over 12 | Used ownership period − 1 (J4323 − 1) for both |
| L39 | B21 | 5267 | Freight distance output omits LPG and LNG trucks | All fuels |
| L40 | B22 | 5368, 5373 | Average gas fuel economy weights freight by LPG freight fuel (5244 for 5245); the EV fuel-economy fallback tests diesel (5326) | The right rows |
| L41 | B23 | 4555 | PHEV TCO includes the full BEV range anxiety (about 100,000 USD per vehicle), so PHEV sales vanish | No range anxiety for PHEVs (user decision 2026-10-14) |
| M13 (L-) | | 2404, 4374 | Prototype: the vehicle feebate counted the carbon price twice (carbon price × coverage on top of a fuel price that holds it) | Feebate + road regulation shadow price |
| M16 (L226) | | 4637 (policy copy 10953) | Freight BEV feebate valued at the ICEV truck's discounted distance (same values in legacy) | Its own distance |
