| All | −18.99 / −30.97 / −43.32 | −22.86 / −35.90 / −49.39 | −17.63 / −30.44 / −45.17 | −82.26 / −77.77 / −76.57 | −4.67 / −11.73 / −12.53 | −2.01 / −6.33 / −4.92 | −2.97 / −4.33 / −4.67 | −20.48 / −36.77 / −52.67 | −26.04 / −42.16 / −57.15 | −6.07 / −6.07 / −6.07 |
:::

**Reading the effects.**

- **B3 (two-sided ownership calibration) dominates.** Egypt's ownership was 55 per 1,000 in 2025 against a Gompertz
  level of 152, so the calibration factor is 0.36 instead of legacy's floor of 1. Passenger ownership reaches 82 per
  1,000 in 2041 instead of 173, and road fuel use is a third lower by 2035.
- **B20 is the largest choice-side fix.** Legacy front-loads used ICEV depreciation, which raises used ICEV costs and
  the EV share; the fix lowers the passenger EV sales share by about 10 points in 2035.
- **B4 has no effect for Egypt**, because ownership still rises after B3.
- **Fixes with no effect for Egypt** (B1, B7, B10, B21, B22) act through policies or fuels that are zero in both Egypt
  runs: distance tax, EV subsidies, charging subsidy, LPG and LNG trucks. The carbon tax does not enter the legacy
  feebate because the road feebate coverage (row 2404) is 0. They matter for other countries and scenarios.

### Open questions and their decisions {#sec-tr-open}

Decided on 2026-10-14 (user: "Go with suggestions and always try to match existing except where there are bugs").

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **B14 freight distance.** The TCO uses Transport1 `average vkt freight` (48,630 km, clamped to at least 50,000 km, binding in every projection year), while fuel use uses 8,091 km (from fuel shares) × 1.70. Which freight distance is right; should the clamp stay? | Kept as legacy; a data decision for later |
| 2 | **B20 direction.** The fix uses the used ownership period (13 years) for the used ICEV depreciation annuity, as legacy does for used BEVs and for used insurance | Confirmed: 12 years for both |
| 3 | **Range anxiety after the fixes.** Transport3 values were solved in another vintage: the calculated 2025 passenger EV share was 0.35% against 0.15% actual (Transport3 records 0.24%); with all fixes 0.09% (B20) | Stored values kept at first, mismatch reported; since then re-solved by goal seek on this model (@eq-tr-rafit, LD63) |
| 4 | **B4 value.** 10% (the legacy 2-3 wheeler value) is a placeholder; no effect for Egypt | Kept |
| 5 | **PHEV TCO** includes the full BEV range anxiety (about 100,000 USD per vehicle), so PHEV sales vanish | No range anxiety for PHEVs (new fix B23) |
| 6 | **Data years.** VAT on vehicles is the 2024 rate, customs the 2024 duties, import shares 2022, bus electricity the 2024 EV stock share. Use the last data year instead? | Kept as legacy |
| 7 | **Calibration factors** (passenger distance × 2.67, then gasoline × 1.23): Transport1 ownership × distance / fuel economy explains only 30-60% of Egypt's road fuel | Reported in the workbook; review the data |
| 8 | **Bus electricity (B6).** The fix scales bus electricity with passenger electricity relative to base passenger energy; an explicit bus EV share may be preferable | As implemented |

**Still open:** the freight distance (B14) and the data years of customs, VAT and import shares (data decisions);
the 10% ownership decline limit; a review of the methodology-note parameters against the legacy values.

### Corrections to the survey of legacy {#sec-tr-survey}

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: corrections to the survey"}
- Transport1 holds 220 countries (880 rows of 4 years), not 221; Transport3 has stored values for 194 countries.
- **B4:** the 2026 jump (P4787 = 59.25 against O = 55.12) is the 7.5% growth cap binding (55.12 × 1.075), not a
  closing-stock mismatch.
- **B2** also hits 2-3 wheelers (4501 = 4487). For freight it has no effect on the TCO distance because the 50,000 km
  minimum binds; the effect shows only through 2-3 wheelers and BEV freight from 2038.
- **B6** also mixes units in bus electricity (5318 adds billion liters of diesel, LPG and gas to billion kWh).
- **B3:** with the data to 2025, actual/expected is 55.1/152.1 = 0.36 (the survey's 57.8/138.9 is the 2024 column used
  by legacy).
- **Not in the survey:** B19 (new BEV maintenance at the ICEV rate), B20 (used ICEV and BEV depreciation periods
  differ), B21 (freight distance output omits LPG and LNG), B22 (gas fuel-economy weights use LPG freight; the EV
  fallback tests diesel); the BEV freight feebate (4637) uses ICEV discounted km (same values in legacy; fixed as
  M16); vehicle shares 2078-2081 use the 2022 distance split in every data year; the Transport3 calibration does not
  hold in this file (open question 3).
- **Dashboard labels:** the charging-station subsidy cells G95:G98 are labelled one row off (start level labelled
  "start year", target level "start level", start year "target year", target year "target level"); the model reads
  them by meaning.
:::

## Implementation in Excel-AI and CPAT Python {#sec-tr-impl}

The engineer model is section 5b of the Excel-AI Mitigation sheet and the block `road` of CPAT Python. The boxes
below hold the implementation notes; the user guides are the
[Excel-AI tab](../CPAT_ai_documentation_html/02_Mitigation_Prototype.html) and the
[CPAT Python blocks](../CPAT_coded_documentation_html/02_How_it_works.html#sec-blocks).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: section 5b layout"}
Section 5b sits directly after section 5 (Transport), headed "5b. Road transport: engineer model and outputs to the
transport co-benefits module", with the summary row `trsum` (road fuel and electricity use of the engineer model, ktoe)
visible when the section is rolled up. When it was built it held 855 rows with year values or parameters, 75 label
rows (a label row names the D:G parameters above every run of rows of one variable that has D:G values; the
ScenarioDefinition rows share one) and 19 heading rows. Row keys are the legacy row numbers (baseline numbering) where
a row reproduces one; other keys name helper rows (`R_TR` in the builder; layout `TR_LAYOUT`). Current row ranges (in
the order of the year):

| Rows | Block | What it computes |
|---|---|---|
| 3539-3542 | Switch and timing | `TrModel`, `tr.sw` (`ENGINEERON`), `tr.dk` data year (Transport1 has the year), `tr.col` years from the base year, `tr.pol` policy scenario (scenario number > 1, fix B1) |
| (after) | Policies | 62 ScenarioDefinition rows by class |
| 3611-3695 | Parameters (D:G) | `trp.*`: lifetimes, depreciation, insurance, maintenance, elasticities, logit $k$, ownership (adjustment, Gompertz, limits, decline), freight distance limits, charging and range anxiety, discount rate, ICE split elasticities, data years, road elasticities and AEI (Inputs), GWh per ktoe, VAT on vehicles, GJ and liters per ktoe, EFs (road, fix B7), base-year energy balance, biofuels, fossil shares |
| 3699-3790 | Key inputs | Transport1 lookups (data years, blank = 0), BEV fuel-economy and charging-cost paths, new BEV fuel economy (Manual inputs), vehicle prices (Transport2, last price carried) |
| 3794-3816 | Derived parameters | Base-year split of road fuel by vehicle type (share, ktoe, billion liters), purchase taxes (customs year), bus fuel of the base year |
| 3820-3836 | Inputs from the model | Road prices incl. new policies (USD per liter), gas, PHEV and freight prices (net of VAT), industrial gas price, population, GDP per capita, lagged GDP growth (fix B2), consumer discount rate |
| 3839-3923 | Data-year derivations | Legacy rows 2038-2137: blends, distance and vehicle shares, freight share and the 2-3 wheeler hump (held `trnc`, `trjc`: last data year, fix B3b) |
| 3924-3989 | Stocks | Opening, trailing average, retirement, after retirement, purchases, data-year adjustment, closing |
| 3990-4000 | Charging and range anxiety | BEV stock, charging subsidy (fix B10), stations, mark-up, EV electricity price, range anxiety |
| 4003-4078 | New fuel economy | Fuel mix, prices incl. the feebate per liter, new fuel economy, CO2 intensity; used vehicles |
| 4081-4123 | Distance for the purchase | Distance tax (fix B1), cost per km, distance per new and used vehicle |
| 4126-4233 | TCO | Discounted km, feebate pivots, taxes (`POLPICK`), subsidies, prices after taxes, depreciation (fixes B8, B8w, B20), insurance and maintenance (B19, M17), fuel, range anxiety (none for PHEVs, B23), TCO per km |
| 4236-4311 | Demand and choice | Gompertz demand with two-sided calibration at the last data year (B3), purchases, logit EV choice, ICE fuel split (B9), vehicles |
| 4363-4428 | Stock fuel economy, uncalibrated use | Opening and closing stock fuel economy, cost per km, distance per vehicle, fuel use before calibration |
| 4429-4441 | Calibration step 1 | Bottom-up base-year use incl. buses (/(1 − bus share), B6b), factor by fuel, distance factors by class (held) |
| 4444-4505 | Calibrated distance and fuel | Distance per vehicle, fuel use, CO2, BEV stock fuel economy, electricity (B8, B21) |
| 4509-4522 | Buses | Passenger fuel and electricity in ktoe, bus fuel and electricity (B6) |
| 4525-4573 | Step 2 and results | Calibration factors by fuel (held), road fuel use by fuel (ktoe), biofuels, electricity, distance, fuel use by class, average fuel economy (B22), vehicles |
| 4576-4616 | Fit and co-benefits | EV sales share calculated − actual (data years); `trq`, `tran.rsh`, other road biofuels and self-generated renewables of the elasticity model |

**Formula rules.** Every calculated row has one formula per row for the base year, 2023-2040 and 2041; 2041 calls a
named LAMBDA (light beige), 2023-2040 hold its body with the arguments substituted (at most 100 characters). Rows whose
base year is data or a held base-year value have their own base-year formula (95 rows); base-year values that a
formula reads from the previous column (the code column) are guarded by `IF` or `N()`. Held values (calibration
factors, base-year distance split, last-data-year values) carry forward from the previous column, so no cell reads a
later column. References are relative in the row (column-relative copy across years and scenario groups).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: names, LAMBDAs and constants"}
- **LAMBDAs** (80 new; `TR_LAMBDAS`, notes in `TR_LAMBDA_NOTES`): ENGINEERON, TRDATA, TRBLEND, OPENING, TRAILAVG,

  RESALE, INSMAINT, FUELKM, TOTAL, TOTALRA, TCOFUEL, LOGITICE, ACTSHARE, REST, ACTORCALC, OWNEXP, GOMPTGT, OWNDEM,
  CLAMPOWN, PLUG, ADDTHREE, TURNOVER, NEWINSTOCK, CROSSRATIO, ICESPLIT, NORMSH, OWNSH, PERTH, OPENFE, STOCKFE, VKTFUEL,
  TWOFUEL, BEVFENEW, BEVFEOPEN, PHEVELE, EMITFUEL, INTENSITY, INTENS0, KTOE, KTOEELE, BUSFUEL, BUSELE, AVGFE,

- **Mapping:** sector labels `pas`, `pau`, `lgt`, `fre`, `cyc`, `bus`; fuel labels `phv`, `bev`, `ev`, `ice`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: ScenarioDefinition rows"}

All ScenarioDefinition ranges end at the last transport row (`MT_END`: Mapping, Variables lookups, `mt_lookup`,
`mt_setting`, the batch emulation; macro constant `MT_LAST` in `CPATScenarios.bas`). The Mitigation search range grows
to row 8000 (`MIT_MAX`, macro `MIT_MAX_ROW`).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: switch wiring"}
- **Section 5:** the elasticity fuel use is the variable `enel`. `ener` = `ROADSWITCH($D, tr.sw, result rows, enel)`;
  D = Inputs column `trpos` (gasoline 1, diesel 2, LPG 3, gas 4, biofuels 6; 0 elsewhere). With Engineer, road
  gasoline, diesel, LPG, gas and biofuels of section 5 are those of section 5b in every year (base year: the
  calibrated value = the energy balance); CO2, revenues, CH4, air pollutants and the totals follow.
- **Section 3 H:** `dem` = `DEMROAD($F, tr.sw, road electricity, previous, multiple)`; F = Inputs_power column `tr`
  (1 for road). From 2023 road electricity demand is the engineer value when switched on (base year: the data).
- **Biofuels:** road biofuels = base year × engine use / base-year use (@eq-tr-bio).
- **No circular reference:** last year's power price (base year: the same year's), last year's GDP growth, the GDP
  level after the feedback (which uses last year's effect); fuel prices do not depend on fuel use.
- **CPAT Python:** the switch is not wired; `road.prepare` refuses `TrModel` = Engineer. In the Python chain the road
  block runs in the year loop and feeds the transport externalities (`externalities.transport`) and welfare.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python: deviations from the reference engine"}
The workbook reproduces the Python reference engine (`transport_model_ref.engine(..., fix=ALL_FIXES)`) exactly; the
deviations are in the inputs it receives from the rest of the model:

- **2-3 wheeler gasoline price:** the road gasoline price incl. new policies (as passenger); legacy row 4438 uses the
  price before new policies, so carbon pricing did not reach 2-3 wheelers.
- **VAT on vehicles:** `VAT_WEO` of the customs year from the domestic price data (Egypt 0.14; the legacy run had
  0.1531).
- **Industrial gas price for LNG trucks:** section 2 industrial price + the road new policies (`POSTTAX`).
- **Biofuels:** biofuels stay a fuel; the engineer emission-factor adjustment for blending is 1, and road biofuels
  scale with engineer gasoline and diesel.
- **Formulas written for the 100-character limit, values identical:** the charging-subsidy ramp as
  start + (target − start) × MIN(1, (year − start year) / MAX(1, target year − start year)) (no division by zero when
  the two years are equal); the cross-TCO ratio of the ICE split uses IFERROR for "other fuels without share" (blank,
  as the reference's guard); the average EV fuel economy uses a helper row (`trafen`); the price-response switch of
  the purchase distance is a 0/1 parameter.
- **Road electricity in the base year** of section 3 H stays the data (the engineer value replaces it from 2023).
- **Python interface:** for the check, `power_model_ref.engine` takes an optional `inp['dem_fixed']` (road demand
  from the engineer model; default behaviour unchanged).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: the workbook against the reference, and the engineer model switched on for Egypt"}
`check_full.py`:

- **Section 5b against the reference engine** (all fixes), with inputs from an independent Python recomputation of the
  input mapping (`tr_inputs`): every row with year values and the side-table parameters (base-year split, purchase
  taxes, bus fuel), scenarios 1 and 2, as shipped and with the Lambdas library over every row: max relative difference
  about 4e-14. With the fitted range-anxiety start values in the check's engine inputs, as in the build: max 8e-14
  (reading legacy Transport3 instead, 272 rows differed by up to 61%).
- **Copied scenarios with `TrModel` = Engineer** (11: copy of 1; 12: copy of 2, carbon tax; 13: + EV subsidy; 14: +
  distance tax; 15: + subsidy, distance tax, feebates, charging subsidy): section 5b against the engine (max 5e-14)
  and the whole model against the Python recomputation with the engine's road fuels and road electricity (iterated to
  the fixed point; max 7e-12). Road fuels of section 5 = section 5b; road electricity demand = section 5b from 2023.
- **Regression:** 0 on every shared output code with the default (Elasticity); new variables reported as added.
- **The scenario-copy test** (copy of scenario 2 with carbon price 0 = scenario 1) skips the row `tr.pol`, as it
  skips the scenario number itself.
- **`trq`, `tran.rsh`** (read by the co-benefits module) compared with the cells they read.
- **CPAT Python** `road.step` matches Excel-AI for scenarios 1 and 2 (test block 3.6).

**Directions for Egypt** (engineer model switched on, scenarios 11-15; 2035 unless noted):

| Scenario | Road fuel use 2035 (ktoe) |
|---|---:|
| Baseline (no carbon price) | 24,580 |
| Carbon tax (scenario 2 settings) | 22,564 |
| Carbon tax + EV subsidy, distance tax, feebates, charging subsidy | 14,177 |

- The EV subsidy raises the passenger EV sales share in 2030 from 0.55% to 3.3%.
- The distance tax cuts passenger distance in 2035 from 285 to 183 billion km.
- The legacy engineer run, with its bugs, gives road fuel use a third higher by 2035 (@sec-tr-effects).
:::
